This is the Summary what have i done
Media Viewer refactor
Core idea
Replaced two separate image/video modals with a single swipeable MediaViewerModal that owns its own media-filtered timeline — matching Element X's pattern. Plain-URI avatar viewing stays in the old ImageViewerModal.

New files
MediaViewerModal.tsx — 10-line atom-read shell; renders nothing when closed so the hook never mounts.
MediaViewerModalContent.tsx — full viewer; owns its filtered timeline via useMediaTimeline.
MediaImagePage.tsx — per-page ImageZoom with encrypted-image caching.
MediaVideoPage.tsx — per-page react-native-video, only loads/plays when the page is active.
MediaEdgePage.tsx — black full-screen loading sentinel.
utils.ts — getMediaKind, getImageContent, getVideoContent helpers.
Swipe UX
Horizontal inverted FlashList with pagingEnabled — index 0 (newest) renders at the right, swipe right → older items.
initialScrollIndex + seeded currentIndex so the tapped event is visible immediately; a fallback scrollToIndex runs once the filtered timeline hydrates and resolves the real index.
Header (sender/date/info) only shows for event pages.
Pagination fix (the critical one)
The eager while (!reachedStart) paginateBackwards(100) loop in useMediaTimeline was dragging the shared room store to the start of history and flooding useRoomTimeline. Fixed by:

Replacing the loop with a single initial paginateBackwards(PAGE_SIZE) and exposing loadMore() + reachedStart.
Removing the useMediaTimeline mount from RoomTimeline — the viewer now owns its own timeline, only mounted while open.
Wiring loadMore through MediaList / FilesList via onEndReached so the gallery grid paginates on scroll instead of upfront.
In the viewer, an effect triggers loadMore exactly when the user lands on the older-edge sentinel.
Edge sentinel
Pages array is [...events, olderEdgeSentinel]. No newer-side sentinel — new items arrive live via the timeline listener.
Sentinel always shows a spinner.
When the user lands on it with reachedStart=true, a 500 ms timer fires a one-time toast ("No older media") and scrollToIndex snaps back to the last event.
While still paginating (!reachedStart), the spinner stays; real items fill in as they arrive.
Payload + atoms
Added mediaViewerPayload = { roomId, initialEventId, initialEvent } in timeline.d.ts. initialEvent seeds the first frame before hydration.
Deleted videoViewerPayload atom and the whole video-viewer-modal/ folder.
Updated ImageMessage, VideoMessage, MediaGallery, ImageInfoBottomSheet, VideoInfoBottomSheet to use the new payload; info sheets now close mediaViewerPayload on reply/forward/delete.
imageViewerPayload stayed for the three avatar callers (Profile, UserProfile, RoomDetails); ImageViewerModal was simplified to avatar-only (no event/info code).
Result
Swipeable image+video viewer with lazy pagination that no longer floods the room timeline, plus a proper end-of-history UX (spinner → toast → snap back).

content.text:
`useMediaTimeline` is triggered — confirmed. The effect at [useMediaTimeline.ts:72-227](src/screens/room-media/hooks/useMediaTimeline.ts#L72-L227) runs whenever `room`/`roomId` is set, and since `MediaViewerModalContent` mounts with a valid `payload.roomId`, it fires on open. Also, `MediaViewerModalContent` doesn't gate any UI on the hook's `loading` — it seeds `events` with `payload.initialEvent` so the first frame shows instantly.

The loader you're seeing is almost certainly **`MediaImagePage`'s own spinner** ([MediaImagePage.tsx:103-115](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaImagePage.tsx#L103-L115)), and here's why it re-fires even after the thumbnail was already cached:

- [MediaImagePage.tsx:29-51](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaImagePage.tsx#L29-L51) — `load` is a `useCallback` with `[content]`.
- `content = getImageContent(event)` is a **fresh nested reference** on every render.
- When the timeline hydrates, the [events memo](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaViewerModalContent.tsx#L74-L77) goes from `[payload.initialEvent]` → hydrated 50-item array. Even for the same `eventId`, the SDK returns a new `EventTimelineItem` object, so `event` ref changes → `content` ref changes → `load` is a new function → the reload `useEffect` at [L53-72](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaImagePage.tsx#L53-L72) fires again, calls `setLocalUri(null)` + `setIsLoading(true)`, and the spinner reappears while the image re-resolves.

Two reasonable fixes — let me know which you prefer:

1. **In `MediaImagePage`** — key the reload on `mxcUrl` (the value) instead of on `content`/`load` (references). Minimal, localized, solves the re-fire for other consumers too.
2. **In `MediaViewerModalContent`** — stabilize event references across hydrations by keeping a `Map<eventId, EventTimelineItem>` and reusing prior references. Fixes the root cause for every per-page component (video too), not just images.

I'd lean toward (1) because it's smaller and defensive — MediaImagePage shouldn't re-decrypt when the content object happens to re-reference but its URL didn't change. Want me to apply it?

content.text:
Good diagnosis now: the loader gate is broken. On open, `mediaItems=[]` → `events=[initialEvent]` → `pages=[event, sentinel]`. The sentinel is rendered from the start, and inverted + paging FlashList is landing you on it. Worse: the scroll effect marks `hasScrolledInitiallyRef=true` on that seeded first render, so it never re-fires after hydration to move you to the tapped event's real index.

Fixing by (a) hiding the sentinel until the hook's first pagination completes, and (b) gating the scroll commit on hydration.

Now it waits for hydration, finds the tapped event's true index in the real list, and commits exactly once.

1. Open → `pages=[initialEvent]`, single page, user can't be on sentinel. 
2. Hook's initial pagination completes → `loading=false`, `events` hydrates, `pages=[...events, sentinel]`.

5. `reachedStart=true` → sentinel removed entirely, last real event is the end.

content.text: Let me look at the whole file once more to verify the flow.

Reworked flow:

**States**
- **`loading=true` (hook's first paginate is in flight)** → `events=[initialEvent]`, `pages=[initialEvent]` only. No sentinel, no FlashList remount yet. User sees the tapped image immediately via the seeded single-item list.
- **`loading=false`** → `events` hydrates to real list; `pages=[...events, sentinel]` if `!reachedStart`. FlashList remounts with `key="hydrated"`, so `initialScrollIndex` is re-applied against the hydrated data and lands on the tapped event's true index. `currentIndex` is force-synced to that index so the header reads correctly before the list emits its first viewability event.

**Swipe-back / pagination**
- Sentinel lives at the older-end of the data. Swiping into it fires `loadMore()` via the existing effect at [L177-L181](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaViewerModalContent.tsx#L177-L181).
- Hook paginates → new older events get inserted **between the last real event and the sentinel** (sentinel keeps its trailing position). FlashList preserves pixel scroll position on data growth by default, so the page the user was on (sentinel) shifts out and the newest item of the new batch slides into view — exactly the "show the first one in the batch" behavior.
- When the user swipes to the next edge after that batch, they hit the sentinel again, `loadMore` fires again.
- When `reachedStart` flips, the sentinel is removed; the last real event becomes the end. Snap-back effect at [L123-L129](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaViewerModalContent.tsx#L123-L129) covers the edge case where the sentinel disappeared out from under the user.

**What's removed**
- `hasScrolledInitiallyRef` and the pre-hydration scroll effect — replaced by the `key`-driven remount.
- `seededInitialIndexRef` — replaced by the hydration-gated `setCurrentIndex(initialPageIndex)` effect.

content.text:
Summary of the change:

**Removed `inverted`.** Data order stays `[newest, ..., oldest, sentinel]`, non-inverted horizontal. So:
- `data[0]` (newest) renders at the left edge; `data[last]` (sentinel) at the right edge.
- Swipe **left** = advance index = go **older**.
- Swipe **right** = go back to newer.
- Tapped event lands via `initialScrollIndex=initialPageIndex` + imperative `scrollToIndex(initialPageIndex)` inside a `requestAnimationFrame` once `loading` flips. FlashList 2.3.0's paging/initialScrollIndex combo is flaky after data grows, so the manual scroll is the reliable path.

**Kept the `key` remount + the sentinel-only-when-hydrated gate** — they don't hurt and they make the mount sequence predictable.

Pagination flow:
1. Swipe left past the oldest event → land on the sentinel at the right end.
2. The existing effect fires `loadMore()`.
3. Hook appends K older events to `events`, sentinel's index moves from M → M+K.
4. FlashList preserves pixel scroll offset on data growth by default, so the page at the user's pixel (previously the sentinel) now shows `events[M]` — the newest of the just-loaded batch. Exactly what you asked for.
5. Swipe further left → hit sentinel again → another `loadMore()`.
6. When `reachedStart` flips, the sentinel is dropped; snap-back effect at [L123-L129](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaViewerModalContent.tsx#L123-L129) covers the case where the user was on it at that moment.

Done:
- `inverted` is back on the FlashList.
- `onViewableItemsChanged` → `onMomentumScrollEnd`. `currentIndex` is now derived from `Math.round(contentOffset.x / SCREEN_WIDTH)`, which only fires when the user settles on a page. No more noisy mid-mount viewability events that could pin `currentIndex` to the sentinel.
- Header (sender/date), `loadMore` trigger on sentinel, and video `isActive` still read from `currentIndex`, so all their behaviors are preserved — just driven off a more reliable signal.

To answer your question: **you do need *some* form of page tracking** because `currentIndex` feeds the header, the `loadMore` trigger, and the video `isActive` prop. But you don't need the viewability callback specifically — scroll-offset math is simpler and doesn't fire until the user actually stops on a page.
